name: Brow slitting / cuts
lead: Brow slitting, also called eyebrow slits or eyebrow cuts, is a grooming style in which one or more thin lines are shaved or trimmed through the eyebrow hair so that a bare strip of skin shows as a short vertical or diagonal gap. People use it as a styling accent: the gap draws attention to the brow and eye area and gives the face a deliberate, edgy look. It is done with a razor or trimmer and does not involve cutting skin.

The style is generally traced to hip-hop in the late 1980s, where Big Daddy Kane is widely named as an early popular wearer, followed by Kriss Kross, Vanilla Ice and, later, Bow Wow and Soulja Boy.[2][3][4] It has returned to fashion several times, including on the Miu Miu spring-summer 2021 runway, and is worn by athletes and pop stars such as Neymar Jr and members of BTS.[3]
Wikipedia's article on eyebrows notes that shaving lines into the eyebrows was a cosmetic trend among some younger people in the 1990s and 2000s.[1] No published studies have examined the style.

angle.text: The slit is a visible styling detail that changes the brow outline and stands out around the eyes. Fashion coverage of Iris Law's diagonal double slits says they elongate her eyes.[3] Because only hair is removed, the effect is temporary and the brow grows back.

paras: The style removes a narrow strip of hair across the brow, most often near the tail or arch, leaving a visible gap. Variations include a single slit, multiple slits, or a diagonal cut; people in the 2015 revival tried one to three cuts in one or both brows.[2] Complex notes that hip-hop communities call these "cuts" and objected to the term "slits".[2]

Complex, citing The Root, traces the look to Big Daddy Kane, and a 2015 article lists Soulja Boy and Bow Wow among its wearers; Jay-Z referenced it on his 1999 song "Do It Again (Put Ya Hands Up)".[2] Another history says Kane wore several cuts in the late 1980s and that Kriss Kross, Vanilla Ice, Luke Perry as Dylan in Beverly Hills 90210, and David Beckham in the early 2000s also wore them.[3] Its roots are described as unclear, and one account speculates it echoes real scars from fights.[3]

In 2015 BuzzFeed reported the trend returning, with Instagram posts under the hashtag #EyebrowSlits.[2] In December 2017 Toronto beauty blogger Menal Khan posted a version she called "boxed brows", which Huda Kattan reposted; Yahoo Life traced it to earlier hip-hop style and noted she did not credit that source.[4]

Miu Miu's spring-summer 2021 show featured models with two cuts in one brow, and Isamaya Ffrench created a similar gapped effect with brow concealer for Poster Girl spring-summer 2023.[3] Wearers named include Neymar Jr, BTS, Zayn Malik and Jason Momoa, whose cut is a real scar.[3]

Brow shaping is long established, and fashions have changed repeatedly: Japanese hikimayu from the 8th century involved shaving or plucking brows and painting them higher on the forehead, Elizabethan high-status women sometimes removed brows entirely, and thin plucked brows returned in the 1920s and 1930s.[1] Modern options include tweezing, waxing, threading, trimming, makeup, microblading and transplants.[1]
Wikipedia describes the brows as important to communication, since mobile brows convey emotions such as surprise, recognition and sympathy.[1]

In some communities the cuts have also signalled gang affiliation, according to Yahoo Life, and Wikipedia mentions a 2008 news report connecting shaved brow lines to gang-related concerns in schools.[1][4] Other coverage treats the cuts mainly as a style choice tied to hip-hop and barbershop design culture, in which intricate clipper work has long been common.[2][4]

Brow slits are generally treated in appearance communities as a style choice rather than a facial-structure change. Discussion of eyebrows in these spaces more often concerns shape, density and the eye area.

card.summary: A shaved gap cut through the eyebrow as a hip-hop-rooted style statement; temporary and cosmetic.
card.note: The hair regrows slowly and may be hard to regrow once cut, per Complex.

quick.overview:
Brow slitting is a grooming style where a thin line of hair is shaved out of the eyebrow. It grew out of hip-hop style in the late 1980s and has returned to fashion repeatedly, including on a Miu Miu runway.

The gap draws attention to the brow and eye area and gives the face a stylised look. It is a styling change, not a structural one.
quick.how: Hair is trimmed or shaved from a narrow strip of the brow with a razor or trimmer, leaving bare skin visible, as a single cut, several, or a diagonal pair. Nothing is done to the skin or follicle, so the gap grows back; barbers also cut them as part of clipper designs.
quick.risks: Shaving carries the usual minor risks of razor use such as nicks or irritation. Complex warns eyebrow hair can be slow to regrow, and some communities have associated the look with gang affiliation, which can matter where school or workplace dress rules apply.
